card.name: Kuku
card.era: Traditional; globalised via Les Ballets Africains after 1958
card.tagline: Manian women's circle dance celebrating return from fishing
card.profile: Kuku (Koukou, Cucu, Coucou) is a rhythm and circle dance of the Manian (Konianka) people of the forest region of Guinea around Beyla, near the Cote d'Ivoire border (Alpha Rhythm Roots; Tontinkan). It was originally played only on djembes - one tuned low in place of dunun - for women to dance on returning from fishing. Today it is one of the most popular West African rhythms, played at festivals and full-moon celebrations at varying tempos (fast in Beyla, slower in Odjene) and now arranged with dunun, shekere and bells (Tontinkan; Leicestershire Music).
card.insight: After Guinea's 1958 independence, the national company Les Ballets Africains toured Kuku worldwide, making it a universal floor onto which dancers add steps from their own ethnic groups (Mande Drum and Dance).
card.image_significance: Women's circle djembe celebration. A representative image shows drum-driven communal movement, often in a circle with vivid textiles — forest region (Manian), Guinea.
